CIRCUIT: five op-amp stages, every one drawn the same way - the inverting (-) lead is the UPPER left lead, the non-inverting (+) lead is the LOWER left lead, the output is the right apex, and a feedback element (a capacitor or an inductor) is routed from the output over the top of the triangle back to the upper-left lead. That feedback routing independently confirms which lead is in- on all five. 24 components, 12 nets.
  Stage A = Op-Amp #2 (417,211), feedback Capacitor #0 1uF, driven by V-DC #5 (5V).
  Stage B = Op-Amp #3 (751,241), feedback Inductor #1 1uH, driven from stage A through Resistor #4 1k. Its + input is the only non-grounded op-amp + input on the sheet.
  Stage C = Op-Amp #14 (322,635), feedback Inductor #10 1uH, driven by I-DC #16 (10A).
  Stage D = Op-Amp #11 (732,548), feedback Capacitor #9 1uF, driven from stage C through Resistor #12 1k.
  Stage E = Op-Amp #20 (726,831), feedback Inductor #19 1uH, driven from stage C through Capacitor #21 1uF.
  A right-hand column at x~996 collects the three output resistors (#6 1k from B, #13 2k from D, #22 1k from E).

JUDGEMENT CALLS
  * S20 (510,535) -> JUNCTION. This is the only genuine wire-on-wire crossing in the drawing: the long vertical that carries Op-Amp #3's + input down from y~345 to y~805 crosses stage C's output rail at y~533. Plain X - no solder dot, no hop, no jog. Pixel dump (inkmap at 512,534): the vertical is 2-3 px throughout and only widens to about 5-6 px for the two rows immediately under the rail, i.e. roughly the union of a 2.5-px vertical with a 4-row-thick sloping horizontal, well short of the ~3x-in-both-axes signature of a real solder blob. Decided junction on the brief's rule 2 (a plain crossing with no hop is a junction in this dataset), with rule 3 contributing nothing because this sheet contains no other wire-on-wire crossing to establish a habit - every other node on it is an unambiguous T. The electrical reading agrees: as a junction, stage C's output fans out to its own 1uH feedback, to stage D via the 1k, to stage B's + input, and to stage E via the 1uF - a coherent differential/fan-out topology. The crossing reading would instead split n5 into {Op-Amp #14 out, Inductor #10 right, Resistor #12 left} and a 2-terminal net {Op-Amp #3 in+, Capacitor #21 left plate}, i.e. it would leave stage B's non-inverting input reachable only through a capacitor, with no DC return path at all, and would make it the one op-amp input on the sheet that nothing drives. That is the weaker reading, but it is the alternative and it is a real one - if this annotation is wrong anywhere, it is here. Net count would be 13 instead of 12.
  * S7 (292,199), S9 (484,219), S10 (661,221), S12 (814,252), S18 (650,531), S19 (394,533), S21 (996,540), S22 (794,543), S28 (229,619), S35 (653,811), S37 (800,830) -> all JUNCTION, recorded explicitly. Every one is an unambiguous deg-3 T verified in its crop: a feedback element's leg (or, at S21, the 2k output resistor) terminating on a through-running wire. Several show a fat pen blob where the stroke turns (S10 is the fattest, ~8 px), which is corner ink, not a decision. There is no opposite pair to pass through at any of them, so 'crossing' is not even expressible.
  Every remaining site is ink from a handwritten value label or from a component symbol and changes nothing: S0/S1/S2 and S16/S17 and S38/S39/S40 are '1uF' text and capacitor plates; S3/S4/S5, S23/S24, S32/S33/S34 are '1uH' text and inductor coils; S11, S13, S25, S42 are '1kOhm' text.
